titre: Explaining a problem and proposing a solution
intro: At work, at school or in daily life, you often need to report a problem clearly, explain its cause and its consequences, and then suggest a solution without sounding aggressive. This lesson gives you the phrases and structures to do it naturally, in speech and in an email.
objectifs: Present a problem clearly and politely (There's a problem with…, I'm afraid…).
Explain the cause and the consequences (because of, due to, as a result, so).
Suggest one or more solutions with could, why don't we, how about, I suggest, if we…
React to a suggestion and agree on the next step.

texte: English speakers often “soften” bad news with I'm afraid, unfortunately, it seems that or I think we have a small problem. This shows that you are calm and want to cooperate, not to blame anyone.

Then describe the problem with precise facts: what, when, since when. The present perfect is very useful for a problem that continues (The printer hasn't worked since Monday) or that has just happened (The client has cancelled the order).

lignes: There's a problem with the delivery.
I'm afraid the report won't be ready on time.
Unfortunately, the system crashed this morning.
It seems that some emails haven't arrived.
We've got a bit of a problem.
We've got a bit of a problem with the budget.
The thing is, the room is too small for 30 people.

sections.titre: Explaining the cause and the consequences
texte: For the cause: because + clause (because the supplier is late), because of / due to + noun (because of the strike, due to bad weather). Due to is more formal and very common in announcements and emails.
For the consequences: so (spoken), as a result, this means that, which means that. “The train was cancelled, which means that I'll be two hours late.”
exemples: The flight was delayed due to a technical problem.
Formal cause: due to + noun.
We can't start the meeting because the projector isn't working.
Because + subject + verb.
The server was down all morning. As a result, we lost several orders.
Consequence in a new sentence.
Two people are ill, which means that we'll need extra help on Saturday.
Which means that links the consequence to the whole idea before.

texte: Suggest a solution with polite forms that leave room for discussion: We could…, Why don't we…?, How about / What about + -ing?, I suggest (that) we…, One option would be to…, If we…, we could…
Be careful with suggest: I suggest that we leave early / I suggest leaving early, but never “I suggest us to leave”. After how about / what about, use -ing: How about calling the supplier?

lignes: Why don't we move the meeting to Thursday?
How about working from home tomorrow?
I suggest (that) we call the client today.
One solution would be to + base verb
One solution would be to hire a temporary assistant.
If we started earlier, we'd finish on time.

exemples: The room is too small. Why don't we book the conference hall instead?
A suggestion in question form.
If we send the documents by email, the client will get them today.
First conditional for a realistic solution.

texte: To accept: That's a good idea. / That sounds good. / That could work. / Let's do that. To express a doubt: That might be difficult because… / I'm not sure that would work. / The only problem is…
To finish, sum up the decision and the next step: So, to sum up, we'll… / OK, so I'll call them and you'll update the file. / Let's meet again on Friday to check.
exemples: That could work, but the only problem is the cost.
Agreement with a reservation.
OK, so I'll contact the supplier and you'll inform the team.
Sharing out the tasks.

sections.titre: In writing: the structure of an email
texte: An email that reports a problem often follows four steps: 1) the context (I'm writing about / regarding…), 2) the problem (Unfortunately…), 3) the proposed solution (I would suggest… / Would it be possible to…?), 4) the next step (Please let me know if this works for you).
Stay factual, avoid direct blame (You didn't send…) and prefer neutral or passive sentences (The documents haven't been received yet).
exemples: I'm writing regarding order no. 4521. Unfortunately, two items were missing.
Context, then the problem.
Would it be possible to send them by Friday? Please let me know if this works for you.
Solution and next step.

formule: I'm afraid there's a problem with… · because of / due to… · We could… / Why don't we…? / How about + -ing? / I suggest (that) we…
prononciation: I'm afraid /aɪm əˈfreɪd/: stress on -fraid; I'm links smoothly to afraid.
In “Why don't we…?”, don't is often reduced: /waɪ dəʊn wi/. The voice goes down at the end, because it is a suggestion, not a real question.
suggest is /səˈdʒest/ in British English (often /səɡˈdʒest/ in American English); stress on the second syllable.
To sound softer, speak a little more slowly and stress the positive words: “That's a GOOD idea, but…”
erreurs: I suggest you to call the client.
I suggest (that) you call the client. / I suggest calling the client.
Suggest + that + subject + verb, or suggest + -ing; never suggest + person + to.
How about to move the meeting?
The flight was cancelled due to the weather was bad.
The flight was cancelled due to bad weather. / … because the weather was bad.
Due to / because of + noun; because + clause.
Why we don't take a taxi?
Why don't we take a taxi?
Question word order: Why don't we…?
We have a problem of delivery.
We have a problem with the delivery.
The printer doesn't work since Monday.
The printer hasn't worked since Monday.
A problem that started in the past and continues: present perfect.

dialogue.contexte: A small travel agency in Dakar. Aïssatou, the manager, and her colleague Julien, from Lyon, discover a booking problem.
lignes: Aïssatou, I'm afraid there's a problem with the group booking for Saint-Louis.
Present perfect: a recent event with a result now.
The hotel has cancelled ten rooms due to renovation work. So twenty people have nowhere to stay.
Oh no. The group arrives on Friday, which means we only have three days.
We could book rooms in the guesthouse next door. It's small, but it's very nice.
That could work. Why don't we also ask the hotel for a discount on the other rooms?
Good idea. I suggest we call them this morning.
OK. So you'll call the guesthouse and I'll speak to the hotel manager. Let's check again at two.
Sharing the tasks and fixing the next step.

mots: issue
There's an issue with the payment system.
a problem or subject that people discuss (more neutral than problem)
solve
We need to solve this problem quickly.
to find an answer to a problem
solution
One solution would be to hire more staff.
a way of solving a problem
due to
The train was late due to snow.
because of
suggest
I suggest that we wait until Monday.
to give an idea for people to think about
option
We have two options.
one of several things you can choose
fix
Can you fix the printer?
to repair something or deal with a problem
postpone
We'll have to postpone the meeting.
to move an event to a later time
workaround
Until it's repaired, here's a workaround.
a way of avoiding a problem without solving it completely
sort out
Don't worry, I'll sort it out.
to deal with a problem successfully

exercices.consigne: Say if the sentence announces a problem (P), explains a cause (C) or suggests a solution (S).
items: I'm afraid the delivery hasn't arrived.
P
It's because of the strike at the port.
C
How about asking another company?
S
The meeting was cancelled due to illness.
C
We could work on Saturday morning.
S

exercices.consigne: Complete with because, because of, due to, so or which means that.
items: The shop is closed ___ the public holiday.
because of (due to)
I can't come ___ my car has broken down.
because
The bus was late, ___ I missed the start of the class.
so
Two drivers are ill, ___ some deliveries will be late.
which means that (so)

exercices.consigne: Rewrite the suggestion with the structure in brackets.
items: Let's change the date. (Why don't we…?)
Why don't we change the date?
Let's take the train. (How about…?)
How about taking the train?
We should call the technician. (I suggest that…)
I suggest that we call the technician.
Hire a temporary assistant. (One solution would be…)
One solution would be to hire a temporary assistant.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: I suggest you to send the file again.
I suggest (that) you send the file again. / I suggest sending the file again.
What about to meet on Thursday?
What about meeting on Thursday?
The internet doesn't work since yesterday.
The internet hasn't worked since yesterday.
There's a problem of the heating.
There's a problem with the heating.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite each direct sentence in a softer, more professional way.
items: The report isn't ready for Friday. (I'm afraid…)
I'm afraid the report won't be ready on Friday.
The flight was cancelled. The weather was bad. (due to)
The flight was cancelled due to bad weather.
Move the meeting to Monday! (Why don't we…?)
Why don't we postpone the meeting until Monday? / Why don't we move the meeting to Monday?
Ask the client what they think! (I suggest…)
I suggest (that) we ask the client's opinion. / I suggest asking the client.

exercices.consigne: Write a short email (5–6 sentences) to a colleague: the projector in the meeting room isn't working and the client presentation is tomorrow. Announce the problem, explain the consequence, suggest two solutions and finish.
items: Model answer

Hi Marc, I'm afraid there's a problem with the projector in the meeting room: it hasn't worked since this morning. This means that we can't show our slides to the client tomorrow. We could book the small conference room, which has a screen. Another option would be to send the slides to the client in advance and present them on a laptop. Could you let me know which you prefer by 5 p.m.? Thanks, Awa

a_retenir: Announce: I'm afraid… / Unfortunately… / There's a problem with…
Cause: because + clause; because of / due to + noun.
Consequence: so, as a result, which means that…
Solution: We could… / Why don't we…? / How about + -ing? / I suggest (that) we… / I suggest + -ing.
Finish: So, I'll… and you'll… / Let's check again on…
